text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- There are no obstacles in the way of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU). France agreed to a deal at the EU summit in Amsterdam on Monday which includes a special resolution about employment.
- Clothing retailer Hennes & Maurtiz's pre-tax profit of over 1.01 billion crowns exceeded even the highest market expectations.

- Telecoms group Ericsson says it will lay off 925 people at its Norrkoping plant where printed boards are produced. However, this number is lower than the 1,400 it said it would make redundant earlier.
- The European Union (EU) might put a Nordic gas grid on its priority list, the Trans-European Network (TEN), and thereby help to finance it. The grid would be supplied by gas from Russia and Norway.

- Swedish insurer Trygg-Hansa risks losing 354 million crowns on its remaining interest in troubled U.S. group Home Holdings. Trygg-Hansa has previously estimated that its link to the U.S. group has cost it around four billion crowns.

- Shares in Swedish fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz rose to a new all-time-high level after the company posted a one billion crown profit in the first six months of its fiscal year. The result was significantly better than analysts had expected.
- Construction company Skanska signed an agreement with The Coca-Cola Company which will mean an annual increase in turnover of 500 million to one billion crowns for Skanska.
- Swedish-Estonia businessman Ivar Boman will return to Estonia to help save the Swedish church there.

- Clothing retailer Hennes & Mauritz posted a 63 percent rise in pre-tax profit for the first six months of its 1996/97 fiscal year. CEO Stefan Persson says the company is constantly working on its purchasing side and logistics in order to keep its prices down.
- Swedish aircraft manufacturer Saab AB and its partner British Aerospace are working in 10 countries to try and sell the JAS 39 Gripen fighter jet.
